speaker: Dunham Sully
text: You here about the ad? You're gripping that paper like it's about to run off.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: {ad}. The ad said bed and board.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: It did. The bed creaks some, and I do the cooking. Decide accordingly.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Dunham Sully. Everybody calls me Sully.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Get to know the town before we head out. Folks around here won't give work or credit to a face they don't know.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Say hello to a few people. I'll be out front of the store.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: When did you last eat?

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Yesterday... I think.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: "I think." Your face already told me.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Here, take this. It's not a loan, not an advance. A hungry hand does no work, that's all.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Buy something that keeps. Beans, hardtack... Don't waste it on sweets.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: No canteen either? Take mine. I'll get another, I lose one every year anyway.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Hah. Now you look a little more human.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Fill it wherever you find water. Nobody buys you a drink in the desert.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Right then. The ranch is out of town. Too far to walk, we'll ride.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: No horse, huh? Take Coal. She's old but she knows the way. Complains less than I do.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Where's your horse? Whistle, it'll come. A good horse doesn't keep its rider waiting.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Follow me. When the road forks, go right... or left. Trust your horse, it knows.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Thirty-one years since I first rode this road.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Martha sat up on the wagon and I walked alongside. We couldn't afford a horse.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: And now?

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Now there's a horse.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: ...No Martha.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Anyway. The chickens are waiting on me, and me on them.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Shh. You hear that?

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: The wind?

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Wind doesn't carry off chickens.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Coyotes. Third night running. To the coop, quick!

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: No gun? Here, my father's pistol. I want it back, mind.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Here we are. A house, a barn, a well, a bunch of chickens and me. We're all a little tired.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Tie up your horse and come in. Sun's about to set.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: That's one! Keep at it!

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Not bad. At your age I hit a chicken every other shot.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: The larder's empty too, I might as well say it. There's game past the hill. Easier to sneak up on at dusk.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: This meat'll last us a week. Take the pelt to the butcher in town, he pays well.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: You're not coming?

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: There are folks in town... I can't look in the eye right now. I'll explain later. Go on.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Back already? The butcher didn't swindle you, did he?

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Come, sit down. It's a long night.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: There's something I need to tell you. You deserve to hear it.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Last month I was riding to the bank. Had the deed on me; needed to show it for a loan.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Three riders came out on the road. The one in front had a red beard. He was laughing.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: What did they take?

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: My wallet. My watch. And the deed.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Whoever holds the deed holds the land, so they say. This house, those chickens, Martha's grave... all of it hangs on a scrap of paper.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Didn't you go to the sheriff?

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: I did. "I don't have the men, Sully," he says. Thirty years I paid my taxes, and he doesn't have the men.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Anyway. Get up early tomorrow. The bank wants its interest, and the barn wants a roof.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Morning. No coffee, it's gone. And the roof leaks.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Give me four hours. I'll pay what I can find; little money, but honest.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Good work. That roof'll hold another ten years... or one winter.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Let's ride into town. I'll talk to the sheriff once more; this time I'll have someone with me.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Let me do the talking. The sheriff likes me.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Well... he used to.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Stop by the bank first. Don't carry cash around; pockets around here empty themselves.

speaker: Şerif / Sheriff
text: Sully. The deed again?

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: The deed again. This time I've got a witness.

speaker: Şerif / Sheriff
text: What good's a witness? Nobody knows where Jack's camp is. Those who do won't say.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Is there a bounty on him?

speaker: Şerif / Sheriff
text: There is. Check the board. Full reward to whoever brings him in alive... but nobody does.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Twenty-five dollars. So my deed isn't even worth twenty-five dollars.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Let's go to the saloon tonight. What the sheriff doesn't know, the bartender does.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Buy a drink at the bar. Then keep quiet.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Keep quiet?

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: People can't stand silence. They'll say anything to fill it.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: {kamp}... I knew it. The old hunters' campsite.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: You don't go at men like that at night. We'll camp halfway and move in at dawn.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Take these. My father's binoculars, my old bedroll and some supper. The bedroll's older than you, treat it kindly.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: At your age I slept on the ground like this too. My back hurt less.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Why are you helping me, Sully? From the very first day.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Couldn't say.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Maybe I'm paying back the help nobody gave me. Maybe I was just looking for someone to talk to.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Eat something, then sleep. I'll keep watch; I can't sleep anyway.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Four of them. One on watch, and he's dozing.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: See the red one? By the fire, standing.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: I want him alive, {ad}. His corpse would give me back the deed, but it can't answer for anything.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: And the others?

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: The others are your call. I'll be with the horses; if I hear shots, I'll come.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Take this lasso too. You know how to tie a man, don't you? If not, you'll learn.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Four men... Jack's by the fire.

speaker: Şerif / Sheriff
text: Red Jack. And alive! Ten years I've waited at this desk for this.

speaker: Şerif / Sheriff
text: Tell Sully... Never mind, I'll tell him myself. I owe him that much.

speaker: Şerif / Sheriff
text: Red Jack... Wish he was still breathing. Still, it's something.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: I think you lost this.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: That's mine... Martha's handwriting, right there in the corner.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Thirty-one years... and a scrap of paper.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Martha would've laughed. "Dunham, don't get so attached to paper," she'd say.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: But you did.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: I did. But not to the paper.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: This ranch's door is always open to you, {ad}. Come whenever you like. I'll even buy coffee this time.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Maybe someday I'll have land of my own.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: You will. But first learn to mend a fence.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: So you're up. Figured you'd sleep till noon like Vance's boys.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Where's Vance?

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: In town. Smelled a "big job". Every year he smells a big job.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: I've sat by this fire thirty years, {ad}. Only thing I ever smell is my own coffee.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Anyway. There's meat in your satchel and the fire's lit. Eat first; a hungry man shoots at the wrong things.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: You should know how many rounds your gun holds in your sleep. The day you have to count, you're already too late.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Go on, see to your horse. Only soul in this world that won't turn its back on you.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Take this brush. A horse won't trust a man who doesn't groom it, and neither will I.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: First time I rode up this ridge I was your age. A borrowed gun in my hand, nothing in my pocket.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Any regrets?

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Regret's a luxury, kid. I'm tired, that's all.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: This is my last winter. Come spring, I'm done. Vance doesn't know, and he'd better not.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: We're out of supplies. Dutch can't hunt and Pete can barely hold a gun. It's on us again.

speaker: Dutch
text: Meat! God bless you, {ad}. We've been eating beans for three days.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Keep the hide, it'll come in handy. There's another job tonight: we're nearly out of cartridges.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Someone has to go into town. My face is on every wall, and Vance says "the boss doesn't go to town".

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: There's twenty dollars on your head. If the sheriff's men look at you for two seconds, they'll know you.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Wear the bandana on the road. But take it off before you walk into a shop: nobody sells to a masked man, they run for the sheriff.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Don't linger near a lawman. Buy, leave, come back. If they know you, don't look back, ride.

speaker: Silas Vance
text: Well, well. The old wolf sent the pup to town, and the pup came back unrecognized.

speaker: Silas Vance
text: Tomorrow morning a mail coach comes through. The mining company's payroll is aboard.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Any guards?

speaker: Silas Vance
text: A driver and a coward. Nobody dies, right, Hollis? He's gone soft with age.

speaker: Silas Vance
text: First turn what's left from the old job into cash. The fence doesn't ask questions. And change your look; your description is on everyone's lips in town.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Don't trust Vance, {ad}. I did, for thirty years.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Nobody dies tomorrow. Promise me.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: I promise.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: The ambush is where the road bends. The coach slows down, and we'll be there.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Cover your face. Don't let the driver remember you.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: You promised.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: ...Never mind. Ride now. We'll talk later.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Nobody died. First clean job in thirty years.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Now scatter. That driver's running for town.

speaker: Silas Vance
text: I counted it. Twice. Half's mine, half's the gang's.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: You are the gang, Silas.

speaker: Silas Vance
text: Exactly, old man. Arithmetic isn't for everyone.

speaker: Silas Vance
text: And I heard something: somebody's quitting come spring. Wonder who that could be?

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: I'm tired, Silas. That's all.

speaker: Silas Vance
text: Tired men talk, Hollis. Men who talk hang.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: The price on your head has grown. Money like that draws hunters; outside town, watch your back.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: I'm going for supplies with Dutch. You scout around.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Hunters... Someone told them where I'd be.

speaker: Dutch
text: {ad}! They're gone. Vance, Pete, all of them.

speaker: Dutch
text: They tied up Hollis. Vance called him a "rat", and he's the one who told the hunters where you were.

speaker: Dutch
text: They rode toward {kamp}. I... I can't come. My leg.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Hollis is by the fire, tied up. Vance's men are around him.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: You came. I thought you wouldn't. So did Vance.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: He's the one who sent the hunters. Sell you, shut me up.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: There are two roads, {ad}. Both get you out of this life.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: You take Vance alive to the sheriff; for him, the sheriff forgives you.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Or you leave Vance be; you go to the sheriff and answer for yourself. Clean, but costly.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: If I were you... No. This time the choice is yours.

speaker: Şerif / Sheriff
text: Silas Vance. Alive. Nobody's going to believe who brought him in.

speaker: Şerif / Sheriff
text: I'm striking the bounty on your head, kid. Don't come to this desk from that side again.

speaker: Şerif / Sheriff
text: Vance... That's one way for it to end. I'm striking your bounty; don't let me see you at this desk again.

speaker: Şerif / Sheriff
text: An outlaw walking in on his own two feet... Now I've seen everything.

speaker: Şerif / Sheriff
text: Your debt is paid. Go, live straight.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: It's over, Hollis.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Over? It's just starting, kid.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Thirty years I sat by a fire waiting for the next job.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Now there's nothing to wait for. Strange. Light.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Where will you go?

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: West. I've never seen the ocean. Maybe I'll catch fish; maybe the fish will catch me.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Find yourself a place, {ad}. A door, a fence, a pot of coffee. The things I never found.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Take this revolver. I won't need it again; I hope you won't either.
